paragraphs.sourceText: Most financial crises have plenty in common: they tend to start in the banking sector and involve excessive borrowing, together with an asset bubble. The 26 crisis of 2008 was no different, with the asset bubble focused on US real estate. But my research suggests this crisis had another 27 cause — that some people in the banking sector were playing or “gaming” the system for their own financial gain.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数金融危机都有很多共同点：它们往往始于银行业，涉及过度借贷以及资产泡沫。 2008年的全球危机也不例外，资产泡沫集中在美国房地产。但我的研究表明，这场危机还有另一个根本原因——银行业的一些人为了自己的经济利益而玩弄或“博弈”这个系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: The game being played had several important features. The first was the deliberate complexity of the financial products at its core. Then there are the 28 biases that permeate decision-making at all levels of the banking industry. Banking often attracts people with certain personality 29 , including those who are overconfident and take excessive risks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正在玩的游戏有几个重要的特点。首先是金融产品的核心故意复杂化。此外，行为偏差也渗透到银行业各个层面的决策过程中。银行业经常吸引具有某些性格特征的人，包括那些过度自信和承担过度风险的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Such people tend to like complexity for its own sake, but they often do not fully understand the 30 of that complexity for the stability of the financial system as a whole. Often they do not care — they are primarily interested in gaming the system to 31 their bonuses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些人往往喜欢复杂性本身，但他们往往不完全理解这种复杂性对整个金融体系稳定性的影响。通常他们并不关心——他们主要感兴趣的是利用系统来最大化他们的奖金。

paragraphs.sourceText: The next element is risk. There are parts of the banking sector that will always be 32 to risk, but many bankers have come to feel immune to its potential impact, because they 33 that, however recklessly banks behave, governments will always be there to bail them out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 下一个要素是风险。银行业的某些部分总是容易面临风险，但许多银行家已经感觉自己不受其潜在影响的影响，因为他们认为，无论银行行为如何鲁莽，政府总会出面救助它们。

paragraphs.sourceText: Gaming in the banking sector seems virtually impossible to 34 . The only effective measure to end it would be to make bankers 35 liable for losses, but no government has ever passed such a law, and no single government could do so on its own, since this would immediately cause their entire national banking sector to move wholesale to another jurisdiction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 银行业的赌博似乎几乎不可能消除。结束这种情况的唯一有效措施是让银行家对损失承担个人责任，但没有任何政府通过过这样的法律，也没有任何一个政府能够单独这样做，因为这将立即导致其整个国家银行业大规模转移到另一个司法管辖区。

paragraphs.sourceText: How Do You Bring a Forest Back to Life?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如何让森林恢复生机？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Five hundred years ago, forests covered much of the Iberian peninsula. But that soon changed. Centuries of wars and invasions, agricultural expansion and woodcutting for firewood and shipping wiped out most of the woods and transformed places like Matamorisca, a small village in northern Spain, into degraded landscapes.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 五百年前，森林覆盖了伊比利亚半岛的大部分地区。但这种情况很快就改变了。几个世纪的战争和入侵、农业扩张以及砍伐柴火和航运摧毁了大部分森林，并将西班牙北部小村庄马塔莫里卡等地变成了退化的景观。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The region’s dry climate and depleted soils would be a recipe for disaster in your average program to replant trees, but for the Amsterdam-based Land Life Company it’s an ideal place. “We typically operate where nature does not come back by itself,” says Jurrian Ruys, its CEO. “We go where there are rougher conditions in terms of weather, with rough or very hot summers.” In Matamorisca, they intervened in 17 barren hectares owned by the regional government and peppered them with their signature device: a biodegradable (可生物降解的) cardboard container they call the cocoon which can hold 25 litres of water underground to aid a seedling’s first year. Around 16,000 trees, including oaks, ashes, walnuts, rowans, and whitebeams, were planted in May 2018, and the company reports that 96% of them survived that year’s burning hot summer without extra irrigation, a critical milestone for a young tree.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 该地区气候干燥，土壤贫瘠，对于一般的树木补种计划来说，可能会引发灾难，但对于总部位于阿姆斯特丹的 Land Life Company 来说，这里却是一个理想的地方。 “我们通常在自然不会自行恢复的地方开展业务，”该公司首席执行官朱里安·鲁伊斯 (Jurrian Ruys) 表示。 “我们会去天气条件恶劣的地方，比如夏季恶劣或非常炎热的地方。”在马塔莫里卡，他们对当地政府拥有的 17 公顷贫瘠土地进行了干预，并在其中布满了他们的标志性装置：一种可生物降解（可生物降解的）纸板容器，他们称之为“茧”，它可以在地下容纳 25 升水，以帮助幼苗的第一年生长。 2018 年 5 月种植了约 16,000 棵树，包括橡树、白蜡树、胡桃树、花楸树和白梁树，该公司报告称，其中 96% 在没有额外灌溉的情况下度过了当年炎热的夏季，这对于幼树来说是一个重要的里程碑。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) “Does nature return by itself?” asks Arnout Asjes, Land Life Company’s chief technology officer, who oversees a mix of drone (无人机) and satellite imagery, big data analysis, soil enhancement, QR (二维码) tagging and site-specific tree configuration designs. “Probably, but it can take decades or hundreds of years, so we are speeding things up.”
paragraphs.translationZh: C）“大自然会自行回归吗？” Land Life Company 首席技术官 Arnout Asjes 问道，他负责无人机和卫星图像、大数据分析、土壤改良、二维码标签和特定地点树木配置设计的组合。 “有可能，但这可能需要几十年或几百年的时间，所以我们正在加快速度。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D) His company belongs to a global movement of organisations trying to save degraded or deforested areas, ranging from fertile tropical lowlands to dry hills in temperate (温带的) regions. Spurred by global biodiversity loss and climate change, these groups are pushing the boundary of how to revive forest cover. “It’s not a theoretical proposition,” says Walter Vergara, a forest and climate specialist at the World Resources Institute (WRI). “It requires the right incentives, the right stakeholders, the right analysis and sufficient capital, but it can happen.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 他的公司参与了一项全球组织运动，该组织致力于拯救退化或森林砍伐地区，范围从肥沃的热带低地到温带地区的干燥山丘。在全球生物多样性丧失和气候变化的推动下，这些团体正在突破如何恢复森林覆盖的界限。 “这不是一个理论命题，”世界资源研究所 (WRI) 的森林和气候专家沃尔特·维加拉 (Walter Vergara) 说。 “它需要正确的激励、正确的利益相关者、正确的分析和足够的资本，但它是可以发生的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) How these factors come together for a particular project — and whether saving destroyed woods is even possible — depends on what kind of ecosystem you have in mind. Secondary forests in the Amazon are different from Texas pines recovering after wildfires or the Arctic timber woods that cover much of Sweden. Each provides different reasons for reforestation programs and each has particular needs. In the dry conditions around Matamorisca and similar areas in Spain, Land Life Company worries about rapid desertification (沙漠化). As its focus is on restoring an ecosystem, it works with organisations that don’t expect their money back.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 对于一个特定的项目，这些因素如何结合在一起——以及是否有可能拯救被毁坏的森林——取决于您想要的生态系统类型。亚马逊的次生林不同于野火后恢复的德克萨斯松或覆盖瑞典大部分地区的北极用材林。每个都为重新造林计划提供了不同的理由，并且每个都有特定的需求。在马塔莫里斯卡周围和西班牙类似地区的干燥条件下，Land Life Company 担心快速沙漠化（沙漠化）。由于其重点是恢复生态系统，因此它与不期望收回资金的组织合作。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) With around 600 hectares replanted around the world since 2015 and another 1,100 planned for this year, the company’s drive fits into the Bonn Challenge, a global effort to restore 150 million hectares of the world’s deforested and degraded land by 2020. That’s an area roughly the size of Iran or Mongolia. By 2030, the goal is to reach 350 million hectares — 20% more land than India. These targets include both the rehabilitation of forested areas that have lost density or look a bit weak (a process known as “restoration” in forestry jargon) and the recovery of forest cover in areas where it was completely cleared (what’s known as “reforestation”).
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 自 2015 年以来，该公司在全球范围内重新种植了约 600 公顷森林，今年计划再种植 1,100 公顷，该公司的举措符合波恩挑战赛的要求，该挑战赛是一项全球努力，旨在到 2020 年恢复全球 1.5 亿公顷的森林砍伐和退化土地。这一面积大约相当于伊朗或蒙古的面积。到 2030 年，目标是达到 3.5 亿公顷，比印度多 20%。这些目标包括恢复密度降低或看起来有点脆弱的森林地区（这一过程在林业术语中称为“恢复”），以及恢复完全被砍伐的地区的森林覆盖（称为“重新造林”）。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) That global target is broken into smaller pieces and takes shape in Latin America as the 20x20 Initiative, an effort to contribute 20 million hectares to the overall goal by initiating small to medium projects with the political backing of governments. Unlike Land Life Company, this region-wide project makes the economic and business case for reforestation, even though they are after biodiversity conservation. “You need to bring in private sector money,” says WRI’s Vergara, who leads the initiative, “and that capital needs to see a return on their investment.” A study he led predicts Latin America would see an estimated net present value of about $23 bn over a 50-year period if it reaches its goal.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 这一全球目标被分解为更小的部分，并在拉丁美洲形成了“20x20 倡议”，该倡议旨在通过在政府的政治支持下启动中小型项目，为总体目标贡献 2000 万公顷土地。与 Land Life Company 不同的是，这个覆盖整个地区的项目为重新造林提供了经济和商业理由，尽管它们是在保护生物多样性。 “你需要引入私营部门的资金，”该倡议的领导者、世界资源研究所的维加拉说，“而且这些资金需要看到投资回报。”他领导的一项研究预测，如果拉丁美洲实现目标，50 年内净现值将达到约 230 亿美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Money can come from timber sales in sustainably managed forests or from harvesting “non-wood products” like nuts, oils and fruits from the trees. You can take note of how much carbon dioxide your forest is capturing and sell carbon credits to companies keen to offset their emissions. Or you can even grow the forest hoping that biodiversity will attract ecotourists who’d pay for lodging, birdwatching tours and meals.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 资金可以来自可持续管理的森林中的木材销售或从树上收获坚果、油和水果等“非木材产品”。您可以记录您的森林捕获了多少二氧化碳，并将碳信用额出售给热衷于抵消其排放的公司。或者，您甚至可以种植森林，希望生物多样性能够吸引愿意支付住宿、观鸟之旅和餐费的生态游客。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Still, these backers are not your high-street bank. Money for the 20x20 Initiative comes mostly from financial organisations with triple goals — a modest return on their investment, environmental benefits and social gains — known as impact investors. Take the German fund 12Tree for instance, one of the 20x20 partners. It put $9.5 million into Cuango, a 1,455-hectare property on the Caribbean coast of Panama that combines a commercial cocoa tree plantation with timber extraction from a sustainably managed secondary forest. With their money, they reforested a former cattle ranch, provided high-quality jobs for the surrounding communities and made a return on their investment.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 尽管如此，这些支持者并不是你的商业银行。 20x20 倡议的资金主要来自具有三重目标的金融组织——适度的投资回报、环境效益和社会收益——被称为影响力投资者。以20x20合作伙伴之一的德国基金12Tree为例。该公司向 Cuango 投资了 950 万美元，这是位于巴拿马加勒比海岸的一处占地 1,455 公顷的地产，将商业可可树种植园与从可持续管理的次生林中采伐木材结合起来。他们用钱重新造林了一个以前的养牛场，为周围社区提供了高质量的就业机会，并获得了投资回报。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Even on land cleared decades ago and currently used by farmers, some crops can coexist with the forest, if you find the right balance. Although not technically reforestation, agroforestry (a system of land use in which harvestable trees or shrubs are grown among or around crops or on pasture land, as a means of preserving or enhancing the productivity of the land) provides an opportunity for small-holder farmers to sustain their livelihoods while adding some forest cover to their farms.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 即使在几十年前被砍伐并目前由农民使用的土地上，如果找到适当的平衡，一些作物也可以与森林共存。虽然从技术上讲不是重新造林，但农林业（一种土地利用系统，在作物之间或周围或牧场上种植可采伐的树木或灌木，作为保护或提高土地生产力的一种手段）为小农提供了维持生计的机会，同时增加了农场的森林覆盖率。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) A global project called Breedcafs is studying how trees behave in coffee farms, hoping to find crop varieties that manage to grow under the shade of trees. Coffee grows naturally in such forests, so copying that in farms is taking the crop back to its roots. “By reintroducing trees in the landscape, we impact positively humidity, rain capture, soil conservation and biodiversity preservation,” says coffee expert Benoît Bertrand, who leads the project from the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development. Bertrand is analysing which of dozens of coffee varieties fits better for this system. A similar approach can be applied to land with cocoa, vanilla and fruit trees.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 一个名为 Breedcafs 的全球项目正在研究咖啡农场中树木的行为，希望找到能够在树荫下生长的作物品种。咖啡在这样的森林中自然生长，因此在农场复制咖啡就是让咖啡回归其根源。 “通过在景观中重新引入树木，我们对湿度、雨水收集、土壤保持和生物多样性保护产生了积极影响，”法国国际发展农业研究中心项目负责人、咖啡专家伯努瓦·贝特朗 (Benoît Bertrand) 说道。 Bertrand 正在分析数十种咖啡品种中哪一种更适合该系统。类似的方法也适用于种植可可、香草和果树的土地。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Not every piece of land is fit for reforestation. Vergara’s partners look for safe investments, and even Land Life Company only runs major projects in what they consider “low-risk” countries. “We tend to avoid large-scale operations in countries in some parts of the Middle East or Africa where the permanence is not secured,” says Ruys.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 并非每块土地都适合重新造林。 Vergara 的合作伙伴寻求安全的投资，甚至 Land Life Company 也只在他们认为的“低风险”国家运营大型项目。 “我们倾向于避免在中东或非洲某些地区的国家开展大规模业务，因为这些国家的持久性无法得到保证，”鲁伊斯说。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) But in the right location, perhaps all you need is time. In the Central Pacific of Costa Rica, the 330-hectare National Wildlife Refuge Barú looks nothing like the cattle ranch it was before 1987, when Jack Ewing decided to turn this large estate into an ecotourism destination. Instead of intervening, a friend told him to let nature have its way. Barú’s former grazing lands are now thriving woods and the property boasts over 150 hectares of secondary forests with no intervention from humans. In the past 10 years, animals such as howling monkeys, scarlet macaws and even migratory cougars have returned to the refuge’s land, boosting tourism and revitalising the ecosystem. Ewing, now 75, explains this success using the words his friend chose three decades ago: “In Costa Rica, when you stop managing the shrubs, the jungle comes back for its revenge.”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: What does self-discipline look like at work? Sometimes, it’s the ability to resist temptation, such as distractions to avoid a particular task. Other times it’s the ability to persist with a task when your energy and motivation seem low.
paragraphs.translationZh: 工作中的自律是什么样的？有时，它是抵制诱惑的能力，例如避免分心以逃避特定任务的能力。其他时候，它是当你的精力和动力似乎很低时坚持完成任务的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: What do you believe about the nature of your own self-discipline? Is it something that runs on internal energy that is spent with use? Or is it something that is bolstered as you apply it and persist?
paragraphs.translationZh: 您对自己的自律本质有何看法？它是依靠内部能量运行的东西吗？或者当你应用并坚持时，它会得到加强吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: Your answer matters, as it determines how much self-discipline you experience. For years, research in psychology pointed to self-control as a resource that is depleted with use and needs to be restored through breaks, rest, or sleep. More recently, however, research points to the importance of mindset. If you view self-discipline as an expendable resource, your willpower tends to fade with use. If you believe that exercising your self-control strengthens and fuels it, that is more likely to be your experience as you resist temptation or push yourself to get something done that is not appealing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你的答案很重要，因为它决定了你的自律程度。多年来，心理学研究指出，自我控制是一种随着使用而耗尽的资源，需要通过休息、休息或睡眠来恢复。然而，最近的研究指出了心态的重要性。如果你将自律视为一种消耗性资源，那么你的意志力往往会随着使用而减弱。如果你相信锻炼你的自制力可以增强并促进它，那么当你抵制诱惑或强迫自己完成一些不吸引人的事情时，这更有可能是你的经历。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you don’t already view self-discipline as a force that feeds itself, what might you do? Reflect on times that you had initial difficulty resisting temptation, getting started on something, or sticking with it, but pushed ahead and accomplished the task or met the goal. That’s the kind of experience we’re talking about with this particular belief about self-discipline, and you’ve already had such an experience, so you’ve shown that it’s possible. When you feel your willpower and motivation fading, remind yourself of those previous experiences and imagine the same happening now.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你还没有将自律视为一种自给自足的力量，你会做什么？回想一下您最初难以抵制诱惑、开始做某事或坚持做某事，但仍继续前进并完成任务或实现目标的经历。这就是我们谈论的这种关于自律的特殊信念的经历，而你已经有过这样的经历，所以你已经证明这是可能的。当你感觉自己的意志力和动力消退时，提醒自己以前的经历并想象现在发生同样的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: What if your experiences have always seemed to indicate that your self-control diminishes with use, and you need breaks to recharge? There’s nothing wrong with that as long as you can afford to take those breaks. If not, remind yourself that not everyone experiences self-discipline as a depletable resource and that your experience might be different if you focus on gathering more energy at this point rather than focusing on how difficult it is to continue or the need for a break.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果您的经历似乎总是表明您的自控力随着使用而减弱，并且您需要休息来充电怎么办？只要你有能力休息，这并没有什么问题。如果没有，请提醒自己，并不是每个人都将自律视为一种会耗尽的资源，如果您此时专注于收集更多能量，而不是关注继续下去有多困难或需要休息，您的经历可能会有所不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: Also, if you know someone who is a role model of self-discipline, picture that person in your situation, persisting in the task. Regardless of how you do it, as you push forward to continue to accomplish progress, be sure to mentally reinforce yourself by taking pride in your ability to exert more willpower as you persist.
paragraphs.translationZh: 另外，如果你认识一个自律的榜样，想象那个人在你的处境中坚持完成任务。无论你如何做，当你继续取得进步时，一定要在精神上强化自己，为自己在坚持过程中发挥更多意志力的能力感到自豪。

paragraphs.sourceText: The benefits of exerting willpower are cumulative. Your self-discipline is akin to a muscle, and each time you resist temptation or persist in a task despite a lack of motivation, you strengthen that muscle, leading to less effort and resistance in similar instances in the future.
paragraphs.translationZh: 发挥意志力的好处是累积的。你的自律就像一块肌肉，每当你抵制诱惑或在缺乏动力的情况下坚持完成一项任务时，你就会增强那块肌肉，从而在未来类似的情况下减少努力和阻力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Smartphones have always posed challenges for parents of teens. From social media apps to excessive screen time, the digital world is as threatening as the physical.
paragraphs.translationZh: 智能手机一直给青少年父母带来挑战。从社交媒体应用程序到过多的屏幕时间，数字世界与现实世界一样具有威胁性。

paragraphs.sourceText: A new study shows that about half of parents of teens are worried about their teens being exposed to explicit content online. This is a valid concern, of course. But there are ways to alleviate the spread of explicit content, from changing the settings in their kids’ phone to monitoring such content with apps like Bark.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项新的研究表明，大约一半的青少年父母担心他们的青少年在网上接触露骨内容。当然，这是一个合理的担忧。但有一些方法可以减轻露骨内容的传播，从改变孩子手机的设置到使用 Bark 等应用程序监控此类内容。

paragraphs.sourceText: Just as alarming, if not more so, is that the amount of time teens spend on social media can lead to anxiety and depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: 同样令人担忧的是，青少年花在社交媒体上的时间可能会导致焦虑和抑郁。

paragraphs.sourceText: Excessive screen time has detrimental effects, for a lot of obvious reasons. Constant media consumption inhibits healthy activities associated with childhood, like spending time outside, exercising, talking to friends and family. If it interferes with sleep, that’s even worse.
paragraphs.translationZh: 出于很多明显的原因，过多的屏幕时间会产生有害影响。持续的媒体消费会抑制与童年相关的健康活动，例如户外活动、锻炼、与朋友和家人交谈。如果它干扰睡眠，那就更糟了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ample research shows too much smartphone use produces significant anxiety, depression, and feelings of isolation in teens. Teens log on to social media or spend time online trying to make connections, but end up feeling more alone and sadder than ever. Faceless communication not only produces feelings of isolation and loneliness but increases instances of online bullying and susceptibility to criminal conducts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大量研究表明，过多使用智能手机会导致青少年出现严重的焦虑、抑郁和孤立感。青少年登录社交媒体或花时间上网试图建立联系，但最终却感到比以往更加孤独和悲伤。匿名交流不仅会产生孤立感和孤独感，还会增加网络欺凌和犯罪行为的可能性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Though I’ve banned most social media, I’ve still battled smartphone time with my own kids. A lot of the time I wish I could throw my kids’ smartphones into the nearest lake. The convenience of communication — when they need a ride home from school after practice, for instance — often feels like it isn’t worth the battle to keep their screen time low and productive, and continue to encourage “real-life” activities outside and with friends and family. I understand the addiction and often tell them I’m not sure how I would have handled having a smartphone as a teen. As an adult, I too, struggle with overuse.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管我已经禁止了大多数社交媒体，但我仍然与自己的孩子们一起使用智能手机。很多时候我希望能把孩子们的智能手机扔进最近的湖里。沟通的便利性——例如，当他们在训练结束后需要乘车从学校回家时——通常会让人觉得不值得为保持低屏幕时间和富有成效而进行斗争，并继续鼓励户外以及与朋友和家人进行“现实生活”活动。我理解这种成瘾现象，并经常告诉他们，我不确定自己在青少年时期会如何处理拥有智能手机的情况。作为一个成年人，我也与过度使用作斗争。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a recent TV interview to promote a new film about a mother and daughter navigating social media use, actress Kate Winslet expressed her view on teens and social media — and her concern mirrors the trends. “I do definitely feel that the world of social media is frightening to parents because we don’t really know what’s there,” she said. “We don’t know how our children are using it. We don’t know the effects that it’s really having on them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 在最近的一次电视采访中，为了宣传一部关于母女如何使用社交媒体的新电影，女演员凯特·温斯莱特表达了她对青少年和社交媒体的看法——她的担忧反映了这一趋势。 “我确实觉得社交媒体的世界对父母来说很可怕，因为我们真的不知道那里有什么，”她说。 “我们不知道我们的孩子如何使用它。我们不知道它对他们真正产生的影响。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I don’t think the US government should regulate social media and teen smartphone use, but it is a vital topic for parents to understand and take seriously. Unfortunately, now, parents don’t just have to worry about real-world dangers, but all the ones sneaking online and the effects they have on teenagers and their mental health.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我认为美国政府不应该监管社交媒体和青少年智能手机的使用，但这是家长需要理解和认真对待的一个重要话题。不幸的是，现在，父母不仅要担心现实世界的危险，还要担心所有潜入网络的危险以及它们对青少年及其心理健康的影响。
